    c * (actualPrimeTupleCoefficient T₁ n₁ : ℝ) *

        actualNormalizedPrimeTupleCoefficient T₁ m₁ n₁ *
        actualNormalizedPrimeTupleCoefficient T₂ m₂ n₂ *
        actualNormalizedPrimeTupleCoefficient T₃ m₃ n₃

mathematical_findings.detail: The unnormalized coefficient is the cardinal of the actual product fiber in the supplied finite ordered-prime-list carrier T. It does not replace that coefficient by a squarefree indicator or change any interval label.

For a nonempty product fiber choose its original representative ps. Every other qs in that same fiber consists of primes and has the same product, so Nat.primeFactorsList_unique gives qs.Perm ps. The fiber is therefore a subset of ps.permutations.toFinset. Its cardinal is at most the length of the full permutations list, exactly ps.length! = m!. Repeated prime factors may duplicate entries of the permutations list; this only strengthens the upper bound.

The uniqueness API itself proves the product is nonzero from all-prime entries; it does not demand an omitted n>0 hypothesis. Empty fibers have coefficient zero. The argument includes m=0, n=0 and n=1; no Nodup, Squarefree, disjoint boxes or separated interval labels are required.

m! is strictly positive for every natural m. Dividing the nonnegative literal cardinal by m! gives a value in [0,1] for every natural n, hence absolute bound one. The only structural premises are that every tuple in T has exactly m entries and all those entries are prime.
For arbitrary T,m,n, multiplying the normalized coefficient by m! recovers the unnormalized coefficient. This identity needs no length or primality assumption, only the automatic nonzero factorial.

The scalar c is arbitrary real, so signed coefficients and an already present repeated-label symmetry factor are preserved. Each of the three group factorials is moved into c exactly once, and three restored-coefficient identities plus commutative ring algebra prove the displayed equality. No extra factorial normalization is introduced.
